Prioritizes featured snippets, AI Overviews, and zero-click search results
Optimizes for passage-level content rather than entire pages
Targets voice search and conversational AI platforms

geo_definition.definition: Generative engine optimization is the practice of optimizing content to appear in the responses generated by AI-powered search engines
key_characteristics: Broader scope than AEO, covering all generative AI platforms
Focuses on visibility across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, Claude, and emerging AI platforms
Emphasizes being cited and referenced in AI-generated responses
Builds on traditional SEO fundamentals while adapting to AI-driven search

worked_example_local_business.note: Invented worked example (no real company): a single garden-supply shop with a small online catalogue. It follows four questions a customer might put to an assistant, from the question to the page change that answers it, then says how the owner would tell whether it worked.

walkthrough.customer_asks: Which compost should I use for tomatoes in pots?
walkthrough.page_that_answers_it: A short how-to page that opens with a one-sentence answer, followed by a small comparison of the composts the shop sells
walkthrough.markup: HowTo for the steps, and Product with Offer for each compost it names
walkthrough.why_an_assistant_can_use_it: The first sentence is a complete answer it can quote, and the comparison gives it the distinction the customer asked for

walkthrough.customer_asks: Is the shop open on the bank holiday Monday?
walkthrough.page_that_answers_it: The visit page, with holiday hours written as plain dated lines rather than an image
walkthrough.markup: GardenStore (a LocalBusiness type) with openingHoursSpecification, including the special hours
walkthrough.why_an_assistant_can_use_it: Dated hours in text match the map listing, so the assistant has no conflict to resolve

walkthrough.customer_asks: Can I return a plant that died within a month?
walkthrough.page_that_answers_it: A returns page whose first line is the yes or no, followed by the conditions
walkthrough.markup: FAQPage for the most common returns questions
walkthrough.why_an_assistant_can_use_it: The answer is not buried under policy wording

walkthrough.customer_asks: What can I plant in a shady, north-facing border?
walkthrough.page_that_answers_it: A guide that lists plants by how much shade they tolerate, each linked to its catalogue page
walkthrough.markup: ItemList of the plants, each item pointing to its Product page
walkthrough.why_an_assistant_can_use_it: Each entry is a self-contained answer with a source link

common_mistakes: Holiday hours posted only on social media, so the website and the assistant disagree
Product pages that tell the brand story before saying what the product is for
worked_example_local_business.how_to_tell_it_worked: Each month, ask the same questions in two or three assistants and note whether the shop is named and which page is cited. Watch catalogue visits from AI referrers in analytics, and remember that most in-store visits leave no click trail.
